decisions.reason: 돌변한 is a sudden hostile turn, which BASE’s “turned” underspecifies; SOL’s “swarmed in from all sides” reverses 사방을 덮쳤다 from covering every direction to an inward rush.
decisions.replacement: The battlefield descended into chaos. At the signal, two hundred martial artists suddenly turned on everyone around them and swarmed in every direction like a pack of wolves.

decisions.reason: BASE flattens 칼날 같은 into a compound; SOL keeps the simile but drops 뿜어져 나왔다.
decisions.replacement: They weren’t quite on the level of Gwak Jun and the assassins we’d fought earlier, but an aura like well-honed blades still poured off them.

decisions.reason: 승산 is the narrator’s side’s odds; SOL’s “they’d” distances Taekyung from the two factions, and “real shot” matches his voice better than “real chance.”
눈이 툭 튀어나온다 is eyes popping out, not merely popping wide.
굵은 is volume/thickness; SOL’s “forceful bout” recasts the vomit as intensity rather than a fast, heavy stream.
아 is a mild catch, not “Damn it”; SOL raises the register without source support.
“his face pale” is a natural English absolute for 창백한 얼굴로; BASE’s “with a pale face” is calqued.
예 affirms 못 믿어?; the blade-sharp joke is the immediate “Yes,” and SOL’s “No” reverses the polarity and the punchline.
칼 같은 대답 naturalizes as “cutting,” but SOL’s “quiet laughter” is not 가벼운 웃음이 번졌다.
decisions.replacement: Hyuk’s cutting answer sent a light laugh spreading through the reconnaissance squad. They’d been frozen stiff by the first large-scale battle of their lives, but they seemed to loosen up a little.

decisions.reason: 움켜쥐었다 is clutching the spear, not tightening a grip already held.
명중시켜야 할 continues the arrow metaphor as a target that must be hit; SOL’s “chosen” drops that.
사람과 … 피 웅덩이도 are two things at his feet; SOL merges them and turns 가득 고인 (a standing pool) into “spreading.”
BASE’s “lump” is stiff for 불덩어리; SOL drops 뜨거운.
decisions.replacement: A hot ball of fire surged up from my gut.

decisions.reason: The choked identification has more force before he throws; SOL’s shorter fragment is not an improvement.
압축시켰다 is the source image; SOL replaces it with “devouring” and adds “in an instant.”
튕겨져 나간다 is a bounce/ricochet, not a generic fly-away.
Adding “The” is churn; the clipped sentence already matches 똑같은 결과다.
뽑아낼 수 있다 is draw out/extract, not produce.
SOL flattens 이름만 다를 뿐 and 기라는 면에서는 동일하다 into “both were qi.”
허허허 is a dry heh-laugh, not italic sarcastic “Ha. Ha. Ha.”
각오도 했다 is preparedness, which “prepared” hits more exactly than “ready.”
흔들리는 동공 as “trembling eyes” is the natural fear collocation; “shaking eyes” is calqued.
Drops the doubled “that” without losing 방금 저거.
SOL erases 입을 열었다; BASE’s “his skin” is vaguer than 피부색.
decisions.replacement: Hyuk opened his mouth with a face drained of all color. As far as skin tone went, he could have passed for a white man.

decisions.reason: 정신 승리에 실패한 is failing to win it in his head; SOL’s “any longer” adds a duration the source lacks.
찾기 시작했다 is the start of the hunt; SOL drops 시작했다.
“worst-case scenario” and “by talking” are the natural English for 최악의 경우 and 대화로 해결하면.
대화 좋지 is clipped; “Talk’s good” keeps Taekyung’s punch, while “Talking’s good” only pads it.
거리가 좁혀졌을 때 is the distance having closed, which “By the time we were within” captures better than making them the agents of closing.
가슴이 벌렁벌렁한다 is heart-pounding; “chest hammer” is a body-part calque.
그냥 그렇게 살았을 거다 is living that way; SOL adds “there” and “gone on.”
SOL inserts “the order” and replaces 기대하는 얼굴 with a generic “looked as though.”
푹 is a deep sigh, not a long one, and “as if the sky had fallen” is the exact 하늘이 무너진 표정.
“bump our odds up by a hair” keeps Hyuk’s colloquial 쥐꼬리만큼; “improve” stiffens it.
생각도 하네 is this thought occurring, not a claim he was “capable of” such thoughts.
피식 is a snort-laugh; SOL genericizes it to “a short laugh.”
죽으러 가냐 is going [there] to die; SOL’s “planning to die” drops the going.
짓눌렀다 is crush, which SOL weakens to “pressed down”; “grew damp” is the natural collocation BASE’s “went damp” misses.
decisions.replacement: A heavy silence crushed the space between us. In that brief interval, my palms grew damp.

decisions.reason: 후우 as Phew/Whew is the same beat; no gain.
호락호락한 놈은 아니다 is “not a pushover,” not “easy mark,” and 돌아간 후에도 is returning to reality.
SOL drops glossary 고수 and 자부한다, which P132’s “No. I was a master” pays off.
최대한 is “as much as possible,” not merely “as I can.”
엄청난 장점 is a tremendous advantage; “massive” is a looser synonym.
보며 is looking at his face, not studying it.
The two range clauses contrast spear-can / sword-cannot; English “but” carries that contrast better than “and.”
스며들었다 is seeping through the body; SOL’s “spread” loses the soak-in image.
노렸다 is aimed at the crown; SOL’s “toward” weakens the targeting.
들어갔다 is the sure hit-call; “This is going in” is that beat, while “This will land” pushes it into the future.
그건 확신이었다 is a nominal punch that SOL turns into “I was certain”; BASE needs the article.
The fragment restates 확신 and 피하지 못할; SOL drops both the anaphora and the object of dodge.
제대로 보이지도 않을 is too fast to see, not “to follow”; SOL also adds “now.”
SOL guts 거력, 어지간한 고수, 견디기 힘들, and 짓눌렀다 into generic “overwhelm most masters.”
들리기 시작 is the sword rising, which lines up with the next thought that it is coming up.
그토록 is “that much,” which SOL overstates as “everything”; BASE’s “and” misses the 는데 contrast.
decisions.replacement: I’d put that much force into it, yet I was the one being pushed back. At my dumbfounded expression, the Head Elder’s smile deepened.

decisions.reason: 머리털이 … 전신을 급습했다 is the whole body; SOL trims it to the stock “my hair stood on end.”
미처 …도 keeps “even,” and 밀리고 있던 is being pushed back, not “forced back.”
나를 향해 is toward me; SOL omits the direction of the flash.
쌍절곤 in Taekyung’s US-English voice is nunchucks, not dictionary “nunchaku.”
섭섭한 소리를 is deadpan “That’s a hurtful thing to say,” not the more theatrical “What a.”
After intervening dialogue, “the rod” keeps the thrown object clear; 투척과 동시에 is the instant of the throw.
끌어안고 is gathering him into his arms; “hauled” is a drag, while “scooped” is the pickup.
범위를 빠져나온 is slipping out of range, not the broader “escaped.”
도망쳐야 is run, and 이곳이 전장 is this place is a battlefield, not “we were on” one.
가득했다 is “full of”; “filled with” is the same sentence with no gain.
마초 아저씨 is a macho middle-aged man; “-looking” softens a trait the source states.
얼굴 가득한 칼자국 is a face covered in sword scars; “crisscrossed” invents a pattern.
외마디 비명 is a single cry; SOL drops 외마디.
주르륵 흐른다 is sweat rolling down; SOL adds “back” and “poured,” while BASE’s “down me” is awkward.
decisions.replacement: Cold sweat rolled down my body.

decisions.reason: 남아 있지 않은 is strength left; SOL deletes 남아.
손 하나 까딱 못 하는 naturalizes as the English “twitch a finger,” and “looked as though he’d suffered” unknots BASE’s awkward “it looked like severe internal injuries.”
날아와 박혔다 is a sword coming flying in; “flew in” is only shorter, not better.
한숨을 푹 is a deep sigh, not a long one, and 말을 이었다 is continued.
너털웃음을 터트렸다 is bursting into a hearty laugh; “laughter” is a needless recast.
보았나 is the rhetorical “Have you ever seen”; SOL deletes that flourish.
박혀 있던 창을 뽑아 들었다 needs both the embedding and the drawing-out; BASE is ungrammatical and SOL drops 박혀 있던.
decisions.replacement: I pulled a spear from where it was stuck among the corpses. Then, with everyone’s eyes on me, I spoke.

decisions.reason: 포위 대형 is the named tactic “encirclement formation,” not the participle “encircling.”
“went like this” is the natural lead-in to a quoted saying; “was this” is stiffer.
